items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Frank Rosolino. That was a very good band, also.

ctx.x: Yeah, he married Kay. Yes, that's right. Frank Rosolino. That was a very good band, also. And I think the guitarists have a Sal Salvador. I'm sure it was. Now Sal, I met Sal in New York. He came down to study with Harry Volpe, and we did -- we hung out quite a bit together. Sal Salvador -- Tal Farlow, Jimmie Raney and myself had a thing; every night we met and we played all night long. This was every night. I would leave home about 12:00 o'clock and I would get home the next day about 9:00 or 10:00. And what…

But some good things came out of that. Jimmie Raney was a tremendous guitarist also. I admired him very much. Tal Farlow was -- whew, he was something else, also. But it was kind of like a mutual admiration society.
